components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. The value is normalized before
            it is stored and returned: surrounding whitespace is trimmed and
            internal runs of whitespace collapsed to a single space, it is
            upper-cased, and common street-type abbreviations are expanded as
            whole words (ST->STREET, RD->ROAD, AVE->AVENUE), e.g. '  12  main
            st ' is stored as '12 MAIN STREET'. An address that is blank after
            normalization is rejected.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
          x-field-extra-annotation: |-
            @jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank
            @org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.AddressValidation
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. The value is normalized to
            E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; an explicit
            leading '+' and country code are kept, otherwise country code '+61'
            is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national
            digits. The result must have 8 to 15 digits after the '+' and is
            stored and returned in that canonical form (e.g. '+61412345678').
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '0412 345 678'
          x-field-extra-annotation: |-
            @jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank
            @org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.TelephoneValidation
        email:
          title: Email
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional, but when present it
            must be a syntactically valid address; the value is stored and
            returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.Email"
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current
            date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allow creating this owner even if another owner already
            has the same lastName and address (normally rejected with 409
            Conflict as a duplicate household). Write-only request flag; it is
            not persisted or returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          default: false
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The canonical region derived from the owner's city using a fixed
                city-to-region table (Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC,
                Brisbane->QLD), or 'UNKNOWN' when the city is not in the table.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>'
                where CITY3 is the upper-cased first three letters of city, LAST3
                the upper-cased first three letters of lastName and NNNN a per-city
                4-digit zero-padded sequence equal to one more than the number of
                owners already in that city when this owner was created.
              type: string
              example: 'LON-SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable shared identifier linking owners that belong to the
                same household (same lastName and address). Assigned when an
                owner is created with 'sharesHousehold' true and joins an
                existing household; all members of a household share the same
                value. Absent for owners that do not belong to a shared
                household.
              type: string
              example: 'a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of owners that already existed, at the moment this
                owner was created, sharing the same firstName and lastName
                (compared case-insensitively). Zero when the owner's name was
                unique at creation time.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>'
                where YY is the last two digits of the registrationDate year.
              type: string
              example: 'LON-SMI-0007-M26'
              readOnly: true
            membershipTier:
              title: Membership tier
              description: >-
                The owner's membership tier. 'SILVER' when the owner's name was
                unique at creation time (namesakeCount is 0) and an email is
                present, otherwise 'BRONZE'.
              type: string
              example: 'SILVER'
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets

Done. The change is implemented and the full test suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 1/1 passing).

## What I did

The response field `bulkSignupWarning` is read back via `GET /api/owners/{id}`, so — matching the existing pattern for creation-time derived fields like `namesakeCount` — I compute it at creation and persist it on the owner.

1. **`ClinicServiceImpl.saveOwner`** — for new owners, set the flag using the same daily-accumulation path as the per-day limit rule:
   ```java
   owner.setBulkSignupWarning(
       countOwnersRegisteredOn(registrationDate) > BULK_SIGNUP_WARNING_THRESHOLD);
   ```
   with `BULK_SIGNUP_WARNING_THRESHOLD = 80`. `countOwnersRegisteredOn` counts owners already registered that day (before this one), so "more than 80 already created today" → `true`, otherwise `false`.

2. **`Owner` entity** — added a `boolean bulkSignupWarning` field (`@Column(name = "bulk_signup_warning")`) with getter/setter.

3. **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `bulkSignupWarning` boolean to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` carries it and MapStruct auto-maps it (verified in the generated `OwnerMapperImpl`).

4. **Schema SQL** (h2, hsqldb, mysql, postgres) — added `bulk_signup_warning BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL` so seed rows and all inserts get a non-null `false` by default (the `DEFAULT … NOT NULL` ordering is what HSQLDB's parser requires).

The acceptance test's default branch (`$.bulkSignupWarning` is `false` for a fresh create) passes, and the `>80` branch rides the same counting path the daily-limit rule already exercises.
